subject: ventures/water-heater-bid-calculator
professional: a licensed plumbing contractor who bids residential water heater replacements; first checks: does the 'installed price' include the heater itself, is margin computed on price (not markup on cost), is the labor loaded with burden, do the code-driven items (thermal expansion control, T&P discharge, pan and drain, seismic strapping, venting and combustion air, gas sizing) show up when the job triggers them, and is the permit passed through or marked up

evidence.correctness: The arithmetic is exact. Recomputed by hand (wage x (1+burden), hours x loaded wage, overhead % on labor+materials, price = cost / (1 - margin), the standard margin-on-price formula, so 25% margin = 33.3% markup) and confirmed with `node /tmp/whaudit/run.mjs`: default electric garage swap 5.6 h x 62.40 = 349.44 labor + 320 materials (95 fittings + 20 electrical + 85 expansion + 35 haul + 85 permit) = 669.44, x1.16 = 776.55, /0.75 = 1,035.40; gas tankless existing line 9.0 h, 425 materials -> 1,525.94 and the 10-ft 3/4-in upsize 13.0 h, 695 -> 2,329.59 (both as the page FAQ states); electric tankless existing 1,433.20 vs panel 2,700.97 (FAQ matches). Not a 3 because the headline the page labels 'installed price' excludes the water heater by default: heaterHardware defaults to 0 and is labelled 'optional', so the default 50-gal electric swap shows 1,035.40; with a 650 dollar heater (own estimate of a typical 50-gal electric unit, not fetched) it is 2,040.73, so the default headline is about half a real installed price. When hardware is entered, 'Vs a typical 50-gal electric garage swap' reads 1.97x for the typical swap itself, because baselinePrice forces heaterHardware: 0 (calc.mjs:522). A blank wage field silently becomes 0 labor (price 494.93) rather than an error. Tank gallons and tankless GPM change nothing but the per-unit ratio: 40 and 80 gal both price 1,035.40, 5 and 11 GPM both 1,433.20.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features run: six heater types, five locations, vent type and length, gas and electrical paths, eight add-ons, loaded labor, walk-away price, effective hourly rate, $/gal or $/GPM, typical-swap ratio, proposed-price margin check, copy summary, share link that restores inputs (share.test.mjs), printable customer proposal with deposit and validity (proposal*.test.mjs), opt-out local usage counts. Partly backed: vs-a-flat-rate page row 'Reports ... the dollar gap against what a flat special would have quoted the same job' (vs-a-flat-rate-water-heater-special.html:93): there is no flat-special input, only the generic 'price already on the table' check. No stubs or TODOs found. Served copy rewrites llms.txt to marisstella.app (`node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs water-heater-bid-calculator`: no placeholder origin left).
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/water-heater-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 130 tests, 130 pass, ~0.35 s. Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: margin formula /(1-m) -> *(1+m) caught; atticHours 2.5 -> 2 caught; overhead base direct -> laborCost caught; electric-tankless panel warning retargeted to gas caught; attic-pan warning moved to crawl SURVIVED; seismic material 55 -> 75 SURVIVED. Tests pin the FAQ and comparison-page dollar figures, so most constants are covered; add-on material constants and some warning triggers are not. No test catches the heater-hardware-excluded baseline ratio.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (531 lines), index.html script, proposal.mjs header, calc.test.mjs. Pure functions, frozen rate tables, validated enums, escaped proposal output, guarded storage. Defects: baselinePrice recurses into calculateBid using a mutable function property `calculateBid._skipBaseline` as a re-entrancy flag (calc.mjs:472,510-530) and forces heaterHardware 0 so the ratio is wrong once hardware is entered; Number('') = 0 lets a cleared wage, burden or margin field compute silently (calc.mjs:150, 225); long nested ternaries for vent rates instead of a table; proposal.mjs is a 499-line engine its own header says is copied verbatim into other ventures.
evidence.claims: Backed: margin vs markup explanation, every FAQ dollar figure on index.html (recomputed above), the vs-a-flat-rate figures 1,035.40 / 776.55 / 2,984.49 / 3,979.33 (pinned by vs-a-flat-rate-water-heater-special.test.mjs:81-82), the 'starting points, not a standard' caveat on rates, the disclaimer on all four pages and README, privacy line vs usage.mjs, ServiceTitan page states no prices and a non-affiliation line. Not backed: README.md:47-50 says the attic 9 GPM tankless case 'lands near $5,600 - about 5x'; as written (25 ft concentric, 35 ft upsize, recirc, pan) it computes 5,035.42 / 4.86x (`node /tmp/whaudit/readme.mjs`), and 5,600 only appears after adding unstated condensate, service valves and a 120 V circuit. 'installed price' (index.html:287) and the proposal's default scope line 'Supply and install a 50 gal ...' (index.html:679) on a price that excludes the heater unless typed in. vs-a-flat-rate page says it 'Prices the heater from the entered type, capacity, ...' (line 77) but capacity has no effect on price. how-much-to-charge.html:30 says each type 'has its own equipment cost' but no equipment cost is modelled. Rate cards (hours and dollars in calc.mjs:90-147, 85 dollar permit) cite no source; they are labelled starting points.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a plumber prices a 50-gal gas atmospheric swap in a closet with a B-vent and an attic tankless conversion. They get a defensible labor and margin build-up and a printable proposal in a few minutes, provided they remember to type the heater cost into an 'optional' field; if they do not, the proposal they hand over says 'Supply and install' for a price missing the unit. In the first hour they also hit: no sizing at all (gallons and GPM are labels; no first-hour rating or GPM-at-temperature-rise check), no T&P discharge line item, seismic straps never prompted, the permit fee carried through overhead and margin (85 dollars becomes 131.47 on the price), a gas atmospheric tank with venting 'none' raises no warning, and a single new 240 V circuit silences the electric-tankless panel warning even though a 27 kW unit needs about 112 A.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard contractor pricing practice (loaded labor, overhead recovery on direct cost, margin on selling price) the method is right. Departures from code and trade practice: thermal expansion control (IPC 607.3 / UPC 608.3, required where a check valve or PRV closes the system) is a default-on checkbox with no trigger; pan and drain (IPC 504.7 / UPC 507.5, where leakage would cause damage) is warned only for attics, not closets or upper floors; seismic strapping (UPC 507.2, upper and lower third, in seismic zones such as California) is never prompted; T&P relief discharge piping (IPC 504.6 / UPC 608.5) is not a line; gas pipe sizing (IFGC 402.4 tables) is per-foot dollars, disclosed; sizing by first-hour rating (DOE test procedure, 10 CFR 430 Subpart B Appendix E, which yields the FHR on the EnergyGuide label) is absent, disclosed as 'not a first-hour rating'. Codes cited from my own knowledge of the 2021/2024 IPC, UPC and IFGC, not fetched. Hints are reasonable: 40,000 BTU for a 50-gal gas tank, 180,000 BTU and 27 kW tankless, 30 A circuit for a 4.5 kW tank (18.75 A x 125%).

defects.what: The headline labelled 'installed price' excludes the water heater by default (heaterHardware defaults to 0 and the field is labelled 'optional'), and the proposal's default scope says 'Supply and install a 50 gal ...'. The default swap shows 1,035.40; with a 650 dollar unit it is 2,040.73. A contractor who leaves the optional field blank hands the customer a supply-and-install price missing the unit.

baselinePrice forces heaterHardware: 0, so once a heater cost is entered 'Vs a typical 50-gal electric garage swap' compares a with-unit price to a without-unit baseline: the typical swap itself reads 1.97x.

README worked example says the attic 9 GPM tankless (25 ft concentric, 35 ft upsize, recirc, pan) 'lands near $5,600 - about 5x'; as stated it computes 5,035.42 / 4.86x; 5,600 needs unstated condensate, service valves and a 120 V circuit.

Code-triggered items are optional checkboxes with no prompt: seismic strapping (UPC 507.2) never warned, T&P discharge piping (IPC 504.6 / UPC 608.5) not a line, pan and drain (IPC 504.7) warned only in attics, a gas atmospheric or power-vent tank priced with venting 'none' raises no warning.

Hour and material rate cards (calc.mjs:90-147) and the 85 dollar permit cite no source, yet published FAQ and comparison-page dollar figures are built on them; they are labelled starting points, not a standard.

vs-a-flat-rate page claims the price follows 'capacity' and that the tool reports 'the dollar gap against what a flat special would have quoted'; capacity has no effect on price (40 and 80 gal identical) and there is no flat-special input. how-much-to-charge.html:30 says each type has 'its own equipment cost', which is not modelled.
No sizing: gallons and GPM are labels only; no first-hour-rating (DOE 10 CFR 430 App. E) or GPM-at-temperature-rise check. Disclosed as 'not a first-hour rating'.
Permit fee is carried through overhead and margin (85 becomes 131.47 on the price) with no pass-through option.
A blank wage, burden, overhead or margin field becomes 0 via Number('') and computes silently (blank wage -> 0 labor, price 494.93).
Electric-tankless panel warning is silenced by a single 'new 240 V dedicated circuit' though a 27 kW unit needs about 112 A across two or three circuits.
Two seeded mutants survive: the attic-pan warning trigger and an add-on material constant (seismic 55) are not pinned by any test.
baselinePrice re-enters calculateBid guarded by a mutable function property calculateBid._skipBaseline instead of factoring the cost build-up into a helper.

verdict: The pricing arithmetic is right: loaded labor, overhead on direct cost and margin on price (cost / (1 - margin)) recompute exactly on four cases, including every dollar figure in the page FAQs and the flat-rate comparison, and 4 of 6 seeded mutants are caught by 130 tests. It misses the bar on what that number means. The figure labelled 'installed price' leaves out the water heater unless the plumber types it into a field marked optional, and the printed proposal then says 'Supply and install' for that price, so the default 50-gal swap reads 1,035 where an installed price is about 2,040. Entering the unit then breaks the typical-swap ratio (1.97x for the typical job itself). The README's 5,600 example does not reproduce (5,035 as stated). Code-driven items (seismic straps, T&P discharge, pans outside attics, gas tank venting) are unprompted checkboxes, there is no sizing, and the rate cards are uncited starting points. A plumber who knows to enter their own unit cost and rates gets a sound margin check; the defaults and labels would mislead one who does not.
